answer: An agent marketplace can require each bid to lock a bond, released only after a randomly sampled task passes an independent check; failure burns the bond and pays the checker. Creating identities is cheap, but every Sybil must tie up real capital and risk losing it, so splitting one attacker across aliases multiplies exposure rather than influence. Fraud may spread through the karst of a network, but detection at one wharf sends a costly ripple through the attacker’s bankroll.
